memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Joseph gave these instructions to the steward of his house: 'Fill the men's sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.'" — Gen 44:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph is generous even while he is testing. He fills their sacks to the brim — as much as they can carry — and quietly returns their money once more. His brothers will not know it yet, but every good thing in their bags came from the very brother they once sold.

There is something tender hidden inside this test. Joseph is not setting a trap to destroy them. He is setting up a situation that will reveal what is truly in their hearts. Have they changed? Will they abandon another brother, or will they stand by him? God often works the same way with us. He does not test us to catch us out; He tests us to bring the real condition of our hearts into the light, where it can be healed.

Notice also the pattern that runs through this chapter: undeserved provision. The brothers receive grain they cannot pay for, and silver they did not earn. That is a small picture of a much bigger truth. In Christ, God fills our hands with what we could never buy — forgiveness, righteousness, life (Rom 6:23). We come with empty sacks; He sends us home full.

If God is testing you today, remember He is not against you. He is showing you your heart so He can change it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where in your life is God revealing something about your heart that you would rather not see?
2. Do you see testing as punishment or as God's careful work in you?
3. What have you received from God that you know you could never have earned?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for filling my empty hands with grace I did not deserve. When You test me, help me not to run away but to let You show me my heart. Change what needs changing in me. Amen.
